title: Policy-backed snapshot scheduler for prompt + metric retention
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a policy-driven snapshot scheduler that creates immutable evidence snapshots (prompts/responses/request logs/metrics) according to per-tenant and per-route retention rules. The scheduler must support: (1) policy expressions (min/ttl/max/triggered snapshot), (2) route/tenant overrides, (3) legal-hold pinning, (4) differential sampling for high-volume telemetry, and (5) exportable signed bundles for audits.

Background: Current retention work covers TTL enforcement and export hooks, but we lack a coordinated snapshot scheduling system that can capture consistent cross-artifact evidence at enforcement points (eg. when a route TTL is about to expire, or before a policy change). This ticket defines the product requirements and acceptance criteria for the scheduler and coordinates eng/design work.

Key requirements:
- Policy semantics: support static TTLs, retention windows, holdUntil, and conditional snapshots (eg. on model rollout or quality regression). Policies should be composable (global -> tenant -> route) with clear override rules.
- Snapshot atomicity: snapshots must atomically include matching prompts, responses, request logs, and related metrics for a configurable time window to enable forensic reconstructions.
- Size & sampling: support deterministic sampled snapshots for high-volume routes (sample rate, stratified sampling by user-cohort, and reservoir sampling options).
- Residency & encryption: snapshot storage must respect tenant residency (region) and encryption keys per tenant (KMS/HSM).
- Export & evidence: exported bundles should be signed (proof-of-origin), include hash chains for integrity, and an index for partial retrieval.
- Scheduling & backfill: the scheduler must support cron-like and event-triggered snapshots, plus a backfill mode for historical buckets.
- Observability: per-snapshot audit logs, duration, size, and retention lifecycle metrics surfaced in Console.

Success metrics:
- Ability to produce a verifiable snapshot for 99% of retention-triggered events in QA cluster.
- Snapshot export generation latency under 60s for <1GB bundles.
- No data residency violations in 100% of sampled exports.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Snapshot atomicity vs. latency: larger atomic windows increase consistency but cost more to store and export. We'll default to 30s atomic windows with opt-in longer windows for critical tenants.
- Sampling complexity: full capture yields highest fidelity but is infeasible for high-volume tenants; provide sampling presets and SDK hooks for deterministic replay.

Open design decisions:
- Default atomic window size (30s vs 60s). Proposal: start with 30s and gather telemetry.
- Default sampling strategy for metrics (stratified by route vs reservoir). Proposal: stratified by route metadata.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Product -> finalize policy DSL and UX (console policy editor + JSON preview).
2) Design -> snapshot bundle schema, evidence index format, and console export UX.
3) Eng -> scheduler service (stateless controller + worker pool), storage adapter (S3/GCS + regional endpoints), signer service integration, and sampling library.
4) QA -> end-to-end tests against seeded telemetry and legal-hold scenarios.
5) Rollout -> beta with 3 pilot tenants, then broader GA.

Deliverables & artifacts:
- Policy DSL spec (Confluence): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Retention+Snapshot+DSL
- Snapshot bundle schema draft (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/snapshot-schema-draft
- UX mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/SnapshotScheduler
- Engineering RFC (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/142

Dependencies:
- ENG-45221 (storage-region-policy-enforcer) for residency checks
- ENG-49990 (signed-export-service) for bundle signing
- DES-73112 (console-policy-editor) for UI surface

Security & compliance:
- Security review required: yes (snapshot contents contain PII-like prompts). Coordinate with Security & Privacy team during design.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy editor exposes snapshot triggers and legal-hold toggles and can save policy version.
- Scheduler produces at least one signed snapshot for a test tenant that includes prompts+responses+metrics and validates hash chain integrity.
- Console shows snapshot audit entry with region and size for pilot tenants.

Rollout plan:
- Beta (pilot tenants): enable via feature flag; collect telemetry and storage cost.
- GA: enable policy migration tools and CLI helpers; publish runbook and evidence export playbook for CSMs and auditors.
